title: Bank Account Struct
story: You're coding a banking app for a school project. Accounts need to accept deposits, process withdrawals, and — most importantly — never let the balance go below zero!
why: Bank accounts are the perfect example of mutation methods — actions that read AND change the struct's internal data.
analogy: A bank account is like a wallet. Deposit adds cash, withdraw takes cash out (but only if you have enough), and transfer moves cash from one wallet to another.
try_it: Add a `transfer` method that moves money from one account to another. It should return `false` if the source doesn't have enough funds. Test it with two accounts.
tips: Always check the balance before withdrawing — guard against negative balances
Return `Bool` from withdrawal to let the caller know if it succeeded
Mutation methods don't need a return type — they change the struct's fields directly
common_mistakes: Allowing withdrawal even when balance is too low — always add the `if balance >= amount` check
Forgetting to use `balance = balance - amount` and writing `balance - amount` instead (no effect)
Confusing the caller by returning nothing from a failed withdrawal — return `false` so they can react
